boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Scranton destinations on campus-adjacent corridors, each with a documented reason to pause and look around.

cards.title: See Scranton’s illuminated landmark
cards.subtitle: Linden Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk Linden Street and frame the sign atop the Scranton Electric Building; the official visitor page places it at 507 Linden Street.
cards.short_summary: A photographed downtown sign mounted above the historic Scranton Electric Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Electric City Sign sits atop the Scranton Electric Building at 507 Linden Street, between Adams and North Washington avenues.
cards.access_notes: Viewable from public downtown streets; do not enter the building for this stop.

cards.entity_name: Scranton Cultural Center at the Masonic Temple
cards.title: Check the marquee and performance calendar
cards.subtitle: North Washington Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Pause outside the Masonic Temple to photograph its façade, then use the venue calendar to choose an all-ages performance if attending.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown performance venue in the city’s cultural district.
cards.evidence_claim: The Scranton Cultural Center at the Masonic Temple is identified by the county visitor bureau as a downtown venue for shows and performances.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is public; ticket and age policies vary by event.

cards.title: Use the square as a civic landmark stop
cards.subtitle: North Washington Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the perimeter and photograph the courthouse setting; check city notices for public programming scheduled on the square.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown civic square used for public events.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Scranton identifies Lackawanna County Courthouse Square as a downtown public-event location.
cards.source_title: Downtown Scranton to Transform into a Vibrant Soccer Haven
cards.access_notes: Public exterior space; event access and setup can change.

cards.title: Photograph the rail-yard setting
cards.subtitle: Cliff Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Approach from the Cliff Avenue side and use the National Park Service’s current visitor information before planning a museum or rail-program visit.
cards.short_summary: A nationally administered railroad-history site in downtown Scranton.
cards.evidence_claim: Steamtown National Historic Site is one of the Scranton historic attractions highlighted by the county visitor bureau.
cards.source_title: Attractions & Things to Do in Scranton
cards.access_notes: Grounds, building access, and programs can have separate hours or fees; verify before entering.

cards.title: Look for the trolley collection
cards.subtitle: Cliff Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the Steamtown-side entrance and photograph the historic-trolley setting; consult the museum before planning an interior visit.
cards.short_summary: A named trolley museum located on Steamtown’s grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: The Electric City Trolley Station & Museum is located on the grounds of Steamtown National Historic Site and interprets Scranton’s trolley history.
cards.source_title: Roadside Attractions & Unique Things to Do
cards.access_notes: Confirm museum access and admission details directly before visiting.

cards.title: Browse the indoor market building
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Enter from the Lackawanna Avenue side to browse the named marketplace’s shops and eateries; individual tenants set their own access terms.
cards.short_summary: A downtown indoor marketplace with multiple shops and food businesses.
cards.evidence_claim: The Marketplace at Steamtown houses shops and eateries under one roof in downtown Scranton.
cards.access_notes: Browsing may be free; purchases and individual business hours vary.

cards.title: Check the film schedule
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Find the Art Haus along Lackawanna Avenue, photograph the marquee, and check its current listing before selecting a screening.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown cinema included in the county’s visitor guide.
cards.evidence_claim: The county visitor bureau lists Scranton Art Haus as a place to catch a movie in downtown Scranton.
cards.access_notes: Screenings require checking current schedules, ticketing, and ratings.

cards.title: Look for the gallery’s current display
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk the Lackawanna Avenue arts corridor and look for the gallery’s current exhibition information before making an interior visit.
cards.short_summary: A named downtown art gallery noted by the county visitor bureau.
cards.evidence_claim: The county visitor bureau identifies Artists for Art (AFA) Gallery as part of downtown Scranton’s arts offerings.
cards.access_notes: Verify exhibition dates and public gallery hours directly before going inside.

cards.title: Take a short downtown park break
cards.subtitle: Lackawanna Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the named city park at 500 Lackawanna Avenue as a quick outdoor pause while walking between downtown destinations.
cards.short_summary: A city-listed park directly on Lackawanna Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Scranton lists Renaissance Park at 500 Lackawanna Avenue in downtown Scranton.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park; observe posted rules and temporary event closures.

cards.title: Follow the gorge-side paths
cards.subtitle: Mulberry Street corridor
cards.notes: Enter via the Mulberry Street approach and follow signed park paths toward the gorge; stay on open routes and observe posted conditions.
cards.short_summary: A named city park with trails, waterfalls, and the Everhart Museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Everhart Museum describes Nay Aug Park as Scranton’s largest park, with hiking trails along the gorge and cascading waterfalls.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park access is generally public; follow closures, trail signage, and seasonal notices.
